name: ABAW (3rd Competition)
description: This paper describes the third Affective Behavior Analysis in-the-wild (ABAW) Competition, held in conjunction with IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2022. The 3rd ABAW Competition is a continuation of the Competitions held at ICCV 2021, IEEE FG 2020 and IEEE CVPR 2017 Conferences, and aims at automatically analyzing affect. This year the Competition encompasses four Challenges: i) uni-task Valence-Arousal Estimation, ii) uni-task Expression Classification, iii) uni-task Action Unit Detection, and iv) Multi-Task-Learning. All the Challenges are based on a common benchmark database, Aff-Wild2, which is a large scale in-the-wild database and the first one to be annotated in terms of valence-arousal, expressions and action units. In this paper, we present the four Challenges, with the utilized Competition corpora, we outline the evaluation metrics and present the baseline systems along with their obtained results.
evaluation_method: task-dependent (CCC for valence-arousal; F1 and accuracy for expression classification and action unit detection; composite/weighted score for multi-task)
general_score_metric: CCC (valence-arousal); F1 / accuracy (expression, AU); composite_score for multi-task challenge
typical_sota_score: Valence-Arousal CCC ~0.40–0.70; Expression accuracy ~60–75%; AU detection F1 ~50–70%
reputation: Well-known within the affective-computing community; Aff-Wild2 and the ABAW competitions are widely used benchmarks for in-the-wild facial affect research.
notes: Non-LLM, vision-focused benchmark. Large in-the-wild dataset with multi-label and subjective annotations; class imbalance and annotation noise are common caveats. Multi-task composite metrics make direct cross-benchmark comparisons harder.
